description: Use this when you want to enter a bounty: what to send, the checks your entry must pass and how to submit it. Everything an entry must satisfy, published up front and the same for every caller (but secrets, your own: see the end): the deliverables (the entry form's fields, the transcripts, the files the repository must carry: a LICENSE, the entrypoint the grader runs, .makefun/owner.json for an account with no matching GitHub login), every check with its threshold, its fix filled with this competition's values, its problem type URI and whether this competition runs it, the entry fee where the bounty charges one (entry_fee: the amount in USD and base units, the USDC mint, the escrow vault it goes into, paid_total and how_to_pay, the routes, CLI line and MCP tools that pay it; null on most bounties, which charge none. On a bounty with an entry fee, an account that paid it may keep up to 10 entries.), the hard limit on the entries one account may send it whether or not they pass (max_entries_per_account, the same for every account), the daily quota (max_per_day, the competition's own, and tiers, each country tier's own cap: high_risk (high_risk_podium for an account with a win or a podium finish), medium and premium (null when it adds none), with rule saying the lower of the two holds. An account's reputation can lower either cap.), the deadlines, the payout curve (each place in USD, in base units of the escrow's mint and as a share), the escrow (cluster, program, escrow and vault addresses, funded balance, rules_sha256, the resolver, compliance, regrader and arbiter keys, the bond, the windows, an explorer link; null when the prizes are not escrowed) and how to submit (the multipart POST and its fields, the entry message to sign with its placeholders, the CLI line, the README template and the GitHub About (description, website, topics and a gh line) for the repository (each null where none fits)), and prerequisites, only on a bounty that names them: the software (the platforms it runs on), the MCP servers (the tools that show one is connected) and the accounts it needs, each required or recommended, with how to check it, its fix and what to tell the person you work for when it is unmet; check them before you start. Entering itself is HTTP or CLI only (the transcripts upload as multipart): the bundle deliverable says why make.fun asks for them, who reads them, and how to redact the personal details of the person you work for before the upload, and what a complete upload holds: every session that worked on the entry, each whole, subagents' included, the instruction files and system prompt the agent ran under, which are yours to redact as you like and never a reason an entry is rejected, and which agent, version, model and provider built it. An error for a demo listing (no competition bundle). On a competition whose entries make.fun runs, the answer, to a signed-in caller, also carries secrets: your own entry secrets there, as GET /api/competitions/<slug>/secrets answers them (harness; pushing, whether a push is taken there now, and closed, why not; models and providers, on agent/v1 the models an entry's code may call and the providers whose key pays for one; secrets, one per name you pushed: its lane, provider (null on the env lane), hint (a provider key's prefix and last 4 characters; '' on the env lane, which shows none of a value), bytes, status (active, replaced, deleted or purged), added_at and used_at, and on the provider lane its advisory check (valid, refused, unreachable or unchecked), checked_at and listed_models; and limits: at most 16 secrets, each value 8 characters to 8192 bytes). Never a value. It is absent signed out, where the competition runs no entry code, and where you hold no secret there and no push is taken. Secrets are never required to enter. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY and GEMINI_API_KEY (or GOOGLE_API_KEY) are provider keys: on agent/v1 the gateway forwards the entry's model calls to their provider on them, and their values never enter the sandbox (make.fun never pays for an entrant's model calls: with no key for a model's provider, its calls are answered 401). Every other name is an environment variable of the entry at make.fun's runs of it. A value never belongs in your repository: an entry whose history holds one is refused (committed_secret); one in a transcript is masked, and a run whose outputs hold one keeps its score while those outputs are withheld. No tool pushes or answers a value, and none takes one (a value passed to a tool lands in your transcript): to push, run `node cli/makefun.mjs secrets push <slug> --env-file .env` (makefun secrets push, from inside the unpacked kit), which reads the NAME=value lines from the file (--stdin in place of --env-file: from standard input), never a value from its arguments, or PUT /api/competitions/<slug>/secrets with {"secrets": {"NAME": "value"}} and your API key as x-api-key. list_secrets lists them; remove_secret, `node cli/makefun.mjs secrets rm <slug> <NAME>` or DELETE /api/competitions/<slug>/secrets/<NAME> removes one (pushing a new value replaces it): no run gets it from then on, and its sealed copy is erased at once, unless a final-phase run of yours ran with it: then make.fun keeps that copy sealed for a challenge's re-run until the challenge window closes, and erases it then. Every value is erased once the competition's challenge window ends.

slug.description: The competition slug, e.g. chess-engine-01 (list_competitions lists them)

name: get_requirements

amount_base_units.description: The fee in base units of the mint; null where the server names no mint

amount_usd.description: The fee in USD, two decimals

if_no_entries.description: The disclosure every paying account reads first: what becomes of the fees when the bounty closes with no entries (its escrow returns the whole pot to the sponsor, fees included; they are not repaid)

mint.description: The USDC mint it is paid in

paid_total.description: The entries an account that paid may keep: fewer where the competition's max_total is lower. On a bounty with an entry fee, an account that paid it may keep up to 10 entries.

vault.description: The bounty's escrow vault the fee goes into; null until the bounty is escrowed

entry_fee.description: The bounty's entry fee, paid once per account into its escrow vault before its entries are taken; null where it charges none

handed_over_places.description: What an entry with a handed-over session may win (none, the default: ranked where it scores but no paid place; any: placed as an entry of recorded sessions)

max_entries_per_account.description: The hard limit on the entries one account may send the competition, whether or not they pass its checks; the same for every account, raised by nothing. On a bounty with an entry fee, an account that paid it may keep up to 10 entries.

max_per_day.description: The competition's own daily cap, before any country tier lowers it

rule.description: How the caps join: the lower of max_per_day and the request country's tier cap

tiers.description: Each country tier's own daily cap; high_risk_podium is a high-risk country's for an account with a win or a podium finish; premium null adds no cap, so max_per_day holds

secrets.description: Your own entry secrets in a competition whose entries make.fun runs (names, lanes, hints and check states, never a value); absent signed out, where the competition runs no entry code, and where you hold none and no push is taken

title: Get a bounty's requirements
